sum: On November 5, 2026: price 3,084.00 GBp, trend uptrend, RSI 70.1, support 2,720.00, resistance 3,084.00. technical analysis of relx stock.

RELX plc closed at 3,084.00 GBp on the London Stock Exchange on Thursday, November 5, 2026, reaching its highest level in the past 20 trading days and ending at the top of that period’s range. The move puts the information and analytics group close to its three-month high, but stretched momentum and subdued trading volume complicate the breakout signal.

The share gained 0.85% on the session, 5.80% over five days and 18.84% over one month, according to the supplied market data. That is a strong advance. But a neutral technical bias means the price strength has not yet been matched by enough indicators to establish a broader bullish confirmation.

RELX is trading above its 20-day simple moving average (SMA), at 2,927.90 GBp, and its 50-day SMA, at 2,701.54 GBp. A share price above both averages generally indicates that recent and medium-term price trends are rising. The 20-day average itself rose 4.01% over five days, reinforcing that direction. No new moving-average crossover was recorded, however, so the latest session did not produce a fresh signal from the relationship between the averages. The close at 3,084.00 GBp is also the 20-day resistance level, placing the price at the top of its recent trading range. The three-month high, 3,129.00 GBp, is just above it. A sustained move through that high would extend the advance; failure to hold the current area could leave the share vulnerable to a pullback toward its moving averages or the 20-day support at 2,720.00 GBp. As shown in the chart, the price is near the upper Bollinger Band at 3,129.54 GBp. Bollinger Bands plot a moving average with upper and lower boundaries based on price variability; the share’s position near the upper boundary shows strong recent demand, but also leaves less room before the price reaches that statistical edge. The band width is 13.8%, described as normal, rather than unusually narrow or expanding.
Momentum indicators confirm the rally but also warn that it has become crowded. The RSI is 70.1, in overbought territory.

RELX stock highlights AI-led STM growth as tools gain traction
sum: RELX is putting artificial intelligence at the center of Elsevier's growth strategy after the scientific, technical and medical division reported faster momentum at an investor seminar. MarketBeat reported on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, that STM revenue growth had reached 6 percent, compared with a previous range of 2 percent to 4 percent cited at an earlier seminar.

Kumsal Bayazit, Elsevier's chief executive, said STM represented 28 percent of RELX revenue and 30 percent of adjusted operating profit in the first half of 2026. The division generated annualized revenue of about 3 billion pounds and adjusted operating profit of more than 1 billion pounds, while roughly 80 percent of its revenue came from subscriptions, according to the report.

Elsevier's growth plan combines scientific content with analytics, workflow software and AI features. Primary Research, including article publishing and research analytics, accounts for slightly more than half of STM revenue, while Decision Support Tools contribute about 40 percent.

Bayazit said Primary Research was growing at a mid-single-digit rate, an improvement from low-single-digit growth four years earlier. Decision Support Tools were also growing strongly as Elsevier added AI capabilities to existing products, launched new tools, combined products into interoperable suites and made its data available within customer workflows.

LeapSpace, an AI-enabled research workspace launched in January 2026, combines Elsevier and third-party full-text material with Scopus data, funding information and customer-provided content. Nearly 1,000 institutions have subscribed, and more than 1 million users have engaged with at least one LeapSpace feature, according to Max Khan, Elsevier's senior vice president for Research Solutions.

In healthcare education, Sherpath AI had reached 100,000 students in 2026, or 20 percent of US nursing students. The platform combines Elsevier nursing content, adaptive quizzes, predictive analytics and AI-supported study tools.

Elsevier is also using its publishing scale to strengthen the evidence base behind its products. The company receives 4.2 million article submissions annually and published more than 800,000 articles in 2025, while accepting fewer than 20 percent of submissions.

RELX stock highlights AI expansion as STM growth reaches 6%
sum: RELX highlighted the growth potential of its Scientific, Technical & Medical division at an investor seminar on Tuesday, November 3, with artificial intelligence at the center of its product strategy. Elsevier Chief Executive Kumsal Bayazit said the division has lifted its revenue growth rate to 6% from the 2% to 4% range discussed at the previous seminar, according to MarketBeat.

STM represented 28% of RELX revenue and 30% of adjusted operating profit in the first half of 2026. Nearly 80% of the division's revenue comes from subscriptions, mainly through multiyear contracts. Primary Research contributes slightly more than half of revenue, while Decision Support Tools account for about 40%.

LeapSpace, Elsevier's AI-enabled research workspace, combines full-text content, Scopus information, funding data and customer materials. Its features include Trust Cards linking findings to source passages and Claim Radar, which identifies evidence supporting, contradicting or producing mixed results around a claim.

In healthcare education, Sherpath AI reached 100,000 students in 2026, equivalent to 20% of US nursing students, according to the seminar account. The platform combines Elsevier nursing content, adaptive questions, predictive analytics and AI-supported study tools. RELX said it aims to expand customer adoption across its modular product suite rather than rely on price increases.

Elsevier receives 4.2 million article submissions annually and published more than 800,000 articles in 2025. Fewer than 20% of submissions are accepted, reflecting the company's emphasis on editorial quality and research integrity as artificial intelligence increases both productivity and the risk of fabricated or low-quality manuscripts.

The company also said it uses more than 120 approved AI models from providers including Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and Mistral. Its technology strategy combines scientific content, extracted information, taxonomies and knowledge graphs to make AI outputs more traceable. Elsevier said it does not use customer data to train its models, while optimization reduced Sherpath AI token costs by nearly 50% during the year as usage increased.

RELX stock keeps full-year outlook after 7% nine-month growth
sum: RELX reported 7 percent underlying revenue growth in the first nine months of 2026 and reaffirmed its full-year outlook in a trading update published on Thursday, October 22. The company said its business mix continues to shift toward higher-growth analytics and decision tools that combine proprietary content with advanced technology.

The SEC filing said RELX expects another year of strong underlying revenue and adjusted operating profit growth, alongside strong adjusted earnings-per-share growth on a constant-currency basis. The outlook is based on continued momentum across the group rather than on a single division.

Legal delivered 10 percent underlying revenue growth in the first nine months. RELX attributed the performance to demand for higher-value legal analytics and tools, strong new sales and adoption of its integrated artificial-intelligence legal research and analytics platform.

Risk grew 8 percent. The division benefited from AI-enabled analytics, financial-crime compliance and digital fraud and identity solutions, while insurance activity was supported by contributory databases, market-specific products and new sales.

Scientific, Technical & Medical revenue increased 6 percent. RELX cited new product introductions, AI-enabled databases and tools, and positive customer feedback for its research-focused AI workspace, LeapSpace. Primary Research was supported by strong growth in article submissions, although the filing did not provide a revenue contribution for LeapSpace.

Exhibitions posted 4 percent underlying revenue growth. The division continued to benefit from its event portfolio, but Middle East disruption moderated the result. RELX still expects strong underlying growth excluding that impact and an improvement in adjusted operating margin compared with the prior full year.

The update reinforces the investment case around RELX's transition from traditional information products toward recurring analytics and decision tools. For shareholders, the key test is whether strong Legal and Risk growth can continue while STM converts product adoption and research activity into revenue and profit.

items.t: Tech stocks fall after AI bosses call for a slowdown in ‘reckless’ progress
sum: Shares of tech companies linked to artificial intelligence (AI) witnessed sharp falls on Monday following calls by AI bosses for a slowdown in the uncontrolled development of the technology. In South Korea, shares of chipmaker SK Hynix fell 6.4% while Samsung Electronics dropped 4.1%. Japan’s Softbank, which is a major investor in OpenAI, plunged more than 10%.
Tech stocks in Europe also followed the trend, as Germany’s Infineon, which designs and manufactures semiconductors, was down 7.6%, while Dutch chip giant ASML fell 5.2%.
The US stock markets also opened down as investors reacted to the calls from tech bosses to slow down the pace of AI development.
The Nasdaq, which is dominated by tech companies, witnessed a big dip in early trading, with shares falling 1.2%.
The S&P 500 followed with a drop of 0.7%, while the Dow Jones was down 0.27%.
As for individula tech shares, Hewlett Packard was down 10%; Intel and Sandisk by 7%; Qualcomm and Micron by 6%, Oracle 5%, and Nvidia fell 3%.
The stocks tumbled after the bosses of Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX called for a slowdown in the “reckless” development, citing fears the technology could soon run out of control.

After Plunging 9.5% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why the Trend Might Reverse for Dover (DOV)
sum: A downtrend has been apparent in Dover Corporation (DOV) lately with too much selling pressure. The stock has declined 9.5% over the past four weeks. However, given the fact that it is now in oversold territory and Wall Street analysts are majorly in agreement about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier, the stock could be due for a turnaround.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.
RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.
However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

The heavy selling of DOV shares appears to be in the process of exhausting itself, as indicated by its RSI reading of 29.03. So, the trend for the stock could reverse soon for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

items.t: Resilient RELX stock steadies as interim dividend and 2026 earnings drive outlook
sum: RELX Plc (GB00B2B0DG97) stock is trading steadily in late August 2026 as investors balance the confirmed 2026 interim dividend against the latest first half 2026 operating picture and sector expectations. As of August 27, 2026, market data from a CBOE-linked venue shows the shares quoted at 2,628.00 GBX, representing a 1.47 percent gain over the last five trading days and a 1.05 percent increase since the start of 2026, signaling a cautiously positive trend rather than a sharp move. This combination of modest price appreciation, a defined cash return to shareholders, and the backdrop of the most recent 2026 earnings figures is shaping the current narrative for RELX stock.

Alongside the share-price context, investors are digesting the company’s 2026 interim dividend decision, which locks in an euro-denominated cash payout per share. Per a recent regulatory summary, the euro equivalent of RELX’s 2026 interim dividend stands at €0.244 per share, providing a tangible income component on top of capital gains potential. With the latest dividend now fixed and the first half 2026 results framing the current operating environment, the equity story turns on whether RELX can continue to translate its information-based analytics and decision tools franchise into steady earnings growth.

The confirmed 2026 interim dividend is a central near-term catalyst for RELX, as it reinforces the company’s policy of returning cash to shareholders while signaling confidence in the underlying business. According to a recent filing summary for 2026, RELX’s interim dividend has been set such that the euro equivalent amounts to €0.244 per share for the current year. This figure slots into the broader multi-year pattern in which the company has progressively grown its distributions, and for income-oriented investors it provides clear visibility on the 2026 cash yield component.

At the current CBOE-linked quote of 2,628.00 GBX as of August 27, 2026, the interim dividend alone implies a meaningful cash return ratio relative to the share price, even before considering the full-year distribution.

items.t: RELX PLC (LON:REL) Just Reported Interim Earnings: Have Analysts Changed Their Mind On The Stock?
sum: It's been a good week for RELX PLC (LON:REL) shareholders, because the company has just released its latest interim results, and the shares gained 2.9% to UK£25.68. It was a credible result overall, with revenues of UK£4.9b and statutory earnings per share of UK£1.12 both in line with analyst estimates, showing that RELX is executing in line with expectations. The analysts typically update their forecasts at each earnings report, and we can judge from their estimates whether their view of the company has changed or if there are any new concerns to be aware of. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on RELX after the latest results.

Following the latest results, RELX's 15 analysts are now forecasting revenues of UK£10.1b in 2026. This would be a credible 3.8% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory per share are forecast to be UK£1.27, approximately in line with the last 12 months. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of UK£10.1b and earnings per share (EPS) of UK£1.27 in 2026. The consensus analysts don't seem to have seen anything in these results that would have changed their view on the business, given there's been no major change to their estimates.

The analysts reconfirmed their price target of UK£33.85, showing that the business is executing well and in line with expectations. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. There are some variant perceptions on RELX, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at UK£50.70 and the most bearish at UK£21.20 per share. Note the wide gap in analyst price targets? This implies to us that there is a fairly broad range of possible scenarios for the underlying business.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. The analysts are definitely expecting RELX's growth to accelerate, with the forecast 7.8% annualised growth to the end of 2026 ranking favourably alongside historical growth of 6.2% per annum over the past five years.

items.t: RELX results suggest 'AI worries look overplayed', Deutsche Bank says
sum: RELX PLC (LSE:REL) is beginning to prove its doubters wrong by showing that artificial intelligence could accelerate growth rather than disrupt its business, although analysts believe further evidence is needed before the shares secure a substantial re-rating.

Following first-half results from the FTSE 100 giant, Deutsche Bank retained its 'buy' recommendation and lifted its target to 3,100p from 3,050p, while UBS reiterated its 'buy' rating and 3,600p price target, implying almost 47% upside from the latest close of 2,451p.
RELX has been one of several data and software publishers hit hard by investor fears that AI could undermine their business models, eroding demand for the subscription products and specialist tools.
But UBS analyst Jo Barnet-Lamb said the results showed "AI-led organic acceleration", with growth at the Scientific, Technical & Medical division increasing to 6% and Legal advancing to 10%.
Adoption of products including LeapSpace and Lexis+ with Protégé continues to rise, supporting what UBS described as a "multi-year growth and upsell opportunity".
Group organic revenue increased 7%, while margins expanded by 70 basis points – well ahead of the 20 basis points expected by analysts.
Deutsche Bank's Steve Liechti said the rapid introduction of products and increasing usage suggested RELX was "only at the beginning of the growth/upside journey".

RELX Shares Climb After Strong H1 Growth and Reaffirmed Outlook
sum: RELX (LON: REL) shares are up over 2% on Thursday after the FTSE 100 information and analytics group posted robust first-half results and reaffirmed its full-year guidance.

The group, which provides data and decision tools across risk, scientific, legal and exhibitions markets, reported revenue of £4,871m for the six months to 30 June 2026, up from £4,741m a year earlier and representing underlying growth of 7%.
Adjusted operating profit rose 9% on an underlying basis to £1,727m, pushing the adjusted operating margin up to 35.5% from 34.8%.

Adjusted earnings per share climbed 11% at constant currency to 68.6p, while reported EPS jumped 24% to 65.7p, aided by a lower net interest charge. The board lifted the interim dividend by 7% to 20.9p, payable on 10 September.

Chief Executive Erik Engstrom highlighted “strong underlying revenue and profit growth and strong new sales” across the group’s divisions, citing continued strength in Risk, a step-up in Scientific, Technical & Medical and Legal, and ongoing strong growth in Exhibitions.

He also pointed to artificial intelligence as an increasingly important driver, saying AI is enabling the company to launch higher value-add products faster while keeping cost growth below revenue growth.

RELX also confirmed progress on capital returns, having completed £1,750m of its £2,250m share buyback programme in the first half, with a further £100m done since 1 July. Net debt stood at £8,733m, equivalent to 2.3 times EBITDA, with cash conversion of 98%.
